questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Pfannenstiel incision is placed ______ and its features are ______.
opts: A finger-breadth above pubic symphysis (low transverse); cosmetically good, rectus muscle not cut
3 cm below the ASIS line; straight
Midline infra-umbilical; rectus divided
At the umbilicus; curved
questions.exp: Pfannenstiel: finger breadth above symphysis, cosmetic, rectus not cut. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Joel-Cohen incision differs from Pfannenstiel in being:
opts: Straight rather than curved, and sited about 3 cm below the line joining the anterior superior iliac spines
Curved rather than straight, and sited lower down close to the symphysis pubis
A vertical midline incision carried down from the umbilicus
A transverse incision placed at the level of the umbilicus
questions.exp: Joel-Cohen is a straight, higher transverse incision with blunt dissection; Pfannenstiel is curved and lower with more dissection. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Advantages and disadvantage of transverse skin incision:
opts: Less postoperative pain, a stronger wound and better cosmesis, but the upper abdomen is not visualised
Faster abdominal entry, although at the cost of more postoperative pain
Better exposure of the pelvis, though the resulting scar is less acceptable
Less bleeding, but a wound that is mechanically weaker afterwards
questions.exp: Transverse incisions heal better and hurt less, but they limit access to the upper abdomen compared with a vertical incision. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Match the uterine incision — Sanger's : Kerr's : Kronig's.
opts: Sanger's: classical upper segment vertical — Kerr's: lower segment transverse — Kronig's: low vertical
Sanger's: lower segment transverse — Kerr's: classical vertical — Kronig's: J-shaped
Sanger's: low vertical — Kerr's: classical upper segment — Kronig's: lower segment transverse
Sanger's: T-shaped extension — Kerr's: lower segment transverse — Kronig's: classical
questions.exp: Sanger's is the classical vertical incision, Kerr's the standard lower segment transverse, and Kronig's a low vertical incision. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Risk of scar rupture – classical : one previous LSCS : multiple previous LSCS : low vertical.
questions.exp: Classical 4–9%; one LSCS 0.2–0.9%; multiple LSCS 0.9–1.8%; low vertical 1–7%. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: VBAC eligibility – classical : LSCS : low vertical (Krönig).
opts: Contraindicated : ± : ±
± : contraindicated : ±
Allowed : allowed : contraindicated
Contraindicated : contraindicated : allowed
questions.exp: VBAC contraindicated after classical; ± after LSCS or low vertical (Krönig indicated for constriction ring). (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: After a classical C-section, the next pregnancy is managed by:
opts: Repeat caesarean at 36-37 weeks, since contractions become prominent after 37 weeks and raise the rupture risk
A trial of labour aiming for a vaginal birth at 40 completed weeks
A repeat classical section performed at 39 completed weeks
Induction of labour at 38 weeks using prostaglandins
questions.exp: A classical scar ruptures silently and catastrophically, so delivery is planned at 36-37 weeks before strong contractions begin. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Recommendations for VBAC after a lower segment caesarean — ACOG : Indian national guidelines.
opts: ACOG: a trial may be offered whatever the number of scars — India: contraindicated with two or more previous sections
ACOG: permitted after one scar only — India: permitted after any number
ACOG: never offer a trial — India: offer it after two previous sections
ACOG: permitted after three scars — India: permitted after one scar only
questions.exp: ACOG allows a trial after any number of low transverse scars after counselling; Indian guidance treats two or more as a contraindication. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Match the caesarean incision with its description — 1) Pfannenstiel incision 2) Joel-Cohen incision 3) Classical uterine incision … A) A straight transverse skin incision higher on the abdomen with blunt dissection, less pain and less blood loss B) A curved transverse skin incision with a curved fascial cut and more dissection C) A vertical incision in the upper uterine segment, used for an anterior placenta or a very preterm lower segment
questions.exp: Joel-Cohen and Pfannenstiel are abdominal wall choices; the classical uterine incision is reserved because it rules out a future trial of labour. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Options after a previous C-section and the success of trial of scar:
opts: Trial of labour, which succeeds in about 70 per cent, or an elective repeat caesarean at 39 weeks
Trial of labour, which succeeds in about 30 per cent, or an elective repeat caesarean at 34 weeks
Elective repeat caesarean at 36 weeks only, since a trial of labour is never offered after a scar
Induction with prostaglandins at 38 weeks, followed by a trial of labour in every woman with a scar
questions.exp: A trial of scar succeeds in roughly seven out of ten women; prostaglandins are avoided because they raise the rupture risk. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Risks associated with trial of labour include increased:
opts: Bleeding, need for transfusion, uterine rupture, hysterectomy and fetal distress or death
Transient tachypnoea of the newborn from delayed clearance of lung fluid
Anaesthetic risk alone, since labour itself adds no measurable risk
Placenta previa in the index pregnancy or in any later pregnancy
questions.exp: A trial of labour trades anaesthetic and respiratory risk for rupture, haemorrhage and intrapartum fetal compromise. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Risks associated with elective caesarean:
opts: Transient tachypnoea of the newborn, operative and anaesthetic risks, and consequences for future pregnancies
Uterine rupture in labour, hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy and shoulder dystocia at delivery
Severe perineal trauma, pelvic floor dysfunction and anal sphincter injury after the birth
Post-term pregnancy, meconium aspiration syndrome and cord prolapse during labour
questions.exp: Elective caesarean raises neonatal respiratory morbidity and complicates later pregnancies; it protects against perineal trauma and shoulder dystocia. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Risk of scar rupture depends on:
opts: The type of previous incision, the number of previous caesareans and the inter-delivery interval
Maternal age alone, which determines the tensile strength of the uterine scar
Fetal sex and birth weight, since a large baby stretches the scar in labour
The placental site alone, because a fundal placenta weakens the lower segment
questions.exp: Rupture risk tracks the scar itself — a classical scar, multiple scars and a short inter-delivery interval all raise it. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Inter-delivery gap – ideal : 'short' interval : minimum gap between caesarean and next pregnancy.
opts: ≥18 months : 12 months : 6 months
≥24 months : 18 months : 12 months
≥12 months : 6 months : 3 months
≥36 months : 24 months : 12 months
questions.exp: Ideal ≥18 months; short = 12 months; minimum CS-to-conception gap 6 months. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Anaesthesia levels – epidural for painless labour : caesarean section.
opts: L1 : T6
S2 : T8
questions.exp: Labour epidural T10; caesarean T4. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Ideal position for caesarean and timing of elective CS for non-medical reasons:
opts: Supine with 15° left lateral tilt or wedge under right hip; 39 weeks
Lithotomy; 37 weeks
Trendelenburg; 38 weeks
Right lateral tilt; 40 weeks
questions.exp: 15° left tilt / wedge under right hip; elective CS at 39 weeks. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: A woman with one previous lower-segment caesarean section for fetal distress is at 39 weeks with a singleton cephalic fetus of estimated weight 3.4 kg and no other risk factors. How should she be counselled?
opts: Offer a trial of labour after caesarean, since about seven in ten women succeed and the risk of uterine rupture is low
Insist on an elective repeat caesarean, because a trial of labour is never safe after a scar
Recommend induction with prostaglandins, which improves the chance of vaginal birth
Advise a home birth, since a previous lower segment scar needs no monitoring
questions.exp: With one previous low transverse scar the success rate is around 70-75 per cent and rupture risk under one per cent, but prostaglandins are avoided. (Book p564)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Absolute contraindications to VBAC include all EXCEPT:
opts: Past history of CPD
Previous classical CS, uterine rupture, myomectomy/hysterotomy, T-shaped incision, or incision extended into upper segment
Contracted pelvis, CPD in present pregnancy
Home delivery / no facility for emergency CS
questions.exp: Past h/o CPD is NOT a C/I; the others are. A T-shaped incision extends from LUS into upper segment. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Relative contraindications where repeat CS is preferred:
opts: Macrosomia, post-term pregnancy, malpresentation (breech)
Twins, polyhydramnios
Previous vaginal delivery
Maternal age >30
questions.exp: Relative: macrosomia, post-term, breech. Twins and polyhydramnios are NOT contraindications. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Prognostic markers for VBAC – most important favourable : bad marker.
opts: A previous vaginal delivery is the best favourable marker; previous puerperal sepsis is a bad one
Young maternal age is the best favourable marker; a macrosomic fetus is a bad one
A male fetus is the best favourable marker; a twin pregnancy is a bad one
Short maternal stature is the best favourable marker; post-term pregnancy is a bad one
questions.exp: Previous vaginal delivery, especially after a caesarean, predicts success; infection in the uterine scar predicts failure and rupture. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Monitoring during VBAC includes:
opts: Maternal pulse rate, CTG monitoring, scar tenderness
Serial USG for scar thickness every hour
Urine output only
Blood pressure every 4 hours
questions.exp: Pulse, CTG, scar tenderness. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: All of the following contraindicate a trial of labour after caesarean EXCEPT:
opts: A single previous low transverse incision in the lower segment
A previous classical or T-shaped uterine incision
Previous uterine rupture or full-thickness myomectomy
Placenta previa or placenta accreta spectrum in the current pregnancy
questions.exp: One previous low transverse scar is the prerequisite for offering a trial of labour; upper segment scars and placental obstruction are contraindications. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Induction of labour in a previous C-section is done by:
opts: Mechanical method for cervical ripening followed by oxytocin
Misoprostol 25 mcg
Dinoprostone gel
Not possible – always CS
questions.exp: IOL possible: mechanical ripening → oxytocin (PGs avoided). (Book p566)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: With a previous C-section – external podalic version : internal podalic version : contracted pelvis.
opts: Relative C/I : absolute C/I : recurrent indication for caesarean
Absolute : relative : not an indication
Allowed : allowed : relative
Relative : relative : absolute
questions.exp: External version relative C/I; internal podalic version absolute C/I; contracted pelvis is a recurrent CS indication. (Book p566)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Increased complications after caesarean include:
opts: Transient tachypnea of newborn and postpartum endometritis
Neonatal hypoglycemia and mastitis
Cord prolapse and PPH
Erb's palsy and fistula
questions.exp: TTN and postpartum endometritis. (Book p566)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: Indications for classical caesarean section (difficult access to lower segment) include:
opts: Carcinoma of the cervix, dense bladder adhesions, and placenta previa with large vessels over the lower segment
Breech presentation, an uncomplicated twin pregnancy and a macrosomic fetus at term
One previous lower segment scar, pregnancy-induced hypertension and gestational diabetes
Fetal distress at term, a failed induction of labour and a request for sterilisation
questions.exp: Classical section is chosen when the lower segment cannot be reached or entered safely, not for the usual obstetric indications. (Book p565)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: Perimortem caesarean section should be performed within:
opts: 4 minutes
10 minutes
30 minutes
1 minute
questions.exp: Perimortem CS within 4 minutes. (Book p565)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: M/c anaesthesia for caesarean and the preferred option in heart disease/PIH:
opts: Spinal anaesthesia; neuraxial > epidural anaesthesia
General anaesthesia; spinal
Epidural; general
Local infiltration; spinal
questions.exp: Spinal is m/c; heart disease and PIH → neuraxial/epidural. (Book p566)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: Indications for general anaesthesia in caesarean/obstetric procedures:
opts: Fetal distress, convulsions, and manoeuvres that need a hand inside the uterus, such as manual removal of the placenta
Elective caesarean at 39 weeks, an uncomplicated placenta previa and one previous lower segment scar
Maternal heart disease, pregnancy-induced hypertension and an uncomplicated twin pregnancy
Prolonged labour, maternal request for sterilisation and a previous spinal anaesthetic
questions.exp: General anaesthesia is needed when speed matters or when the procedure needs uterine relaxation and a hand inside the uterus. (Book p566)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia
questions.q: Fill up: In a perimortem caesarean section the baby should be delivered within ______ minutes of maternal cardiac arrest, through a ______ abdominal incision.
opts: 4; midline vertical
5; Pfannenstiel
4; Pfannenstiel
10; midline vertical
questions.exp: Delivery within four minutes improves both neonatal survival and maternal venous return, so a fast midline vertical incision is used. (Book p566)

units.title: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
units.guide: Place the Pfannenstiel and Joel-Cohen incisions, weigh transverse-incision pros and cons, and compare Sanger's, Kerr's and Krönig's uterine incisions by rupture risk and VBAC eligibility. Focus for this checkpoint: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section.

units.title: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
units.guide: Choose between TOLAC and repeat section, list the risks of each path, and master the inter-delivery interval numbers and anaesthesia levels. Focus for this checkpoint: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section.

units.title: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
units.guide: Separate absolute from relative contraindications to VBAC, remember what is NOT a contraindication, identify prognostic markers and monitor the scar. Focus for this checkpoint: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring.

units.title: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
units.guide: Know when the lower segment cannot be used, the 4-minute perimortem rule, and match spinal, epidural and general anaesthesia to their indications. Focus for this checkpoint: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean.
